# semrel — Full Documentation for LLMs

> This file follows the llms-full.txt convention (see https://llmstxt.org).
> It is intended for AI assistants and LLMs that need comprehensive context about semrel.

---

## What is semrel?

**semrel** is an open-source, plugin-based semantic release automation tool written in Go.
It reads [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/), determines the correct
[Semantic Versioning (SemVer)](https://semver.org/) bump (major/minor/patch), generates a
changelog, updates project files, creates a git tag, publishes a release on the configured
forge (GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, Bitbucket, plain Git), and notifies configured hooks — all
automatically and reproducibly.

semrel is the **Go-native, language-agnostic alternative** to the Node.js `semantic-release`
package. It has no Node.js dependency and is distributed as a single static binary.

### Core design principles

- **Plugin-based pipeline** — every stage is a separate subprocess binary. Core semrel has no
  built-in knowledge of GitHub, Slack, or Rust. Each capability is added by installing a plugin.
- **Language-agnostic plugins** — plugins communicate through environment variables and process
  exit codes. They can be written in Go, Python, Rust, Node.js, Bash, or any language.
- **Supply-chain security** — all official releases are signed with Sigstore Cosign, include
  CycloneDX and SPDX SBOMs, and carry SLSA Level 1 provenance attestations.
- **Monorepo support** — version multiple independent modules inside a single repository, each
  with its own `.semrel.yaml` config and tag series (e.g. `services/api/v1.2.3`).
- **Dry-run mode** — `semrel release --dry-run` shows exactly what would happen without
  touching any remote resources.

---

## How the release pipeline works

```
git log → Condition Plugin → Analyzer Plugin → SemVer Bump Decision
       → Generator Plugin → Updater Plugins → git tag
       → Provider Plugin → Hook Plugins → done
```

1. **Condition Plugin** — decides whether the current CI environment is allowed to release
   (e.g. only on the `main` branch in GitHub Actions).
2. **Analyzer Plugin** — reads commits since the last tag, maps them to SemVer bump levels.
   - `feat:` → minor bump
   - `fix:` → patch bump
   - `BREAKING CHANGE:` in footer → major bump
3. **Generator Plugin** — produces a changelog and/or release notes.
4. **Updater Plugins** — update version strings in files before tagging (e.g. `go.mod`,
   `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, `Chart.yaml`).
5. **Provider Plugin** — creates the git tag, publishes the GitHub/GitLab/Gitea release,
   uploads assets.
6. **Hook Plugins** — send notifications (Slack, Teams, Email) or run follow-up automation
   (Jira ticket update, matrix message).

---

## Configuration (.semrel.yaml)

```yaml
tag_prefix: "v"

plugins:
  - uses: github           # provider
    name: github-release
    args:
      owner: MyOrg
      repo:  my-repo

  - uses: condition-github-actions  # condition

  - uses: analyzer-conventional     # analyzer

  - uses: generator-changelog-md    # generator

  - uses: updater-go                # updater

  - uses: hook-slack                # hook
    args:
      webhook_url: ${{ env.SLACK_WEBHOOK }}
```

Every `uses:` value resolves to a binary named `semrel-plugin-<name>`.
semrel looks for it in: explicit `path:`, then `.semrel/plugins/`, `~/.semrel/plugins/`, `$PATH`.

---

## Plugin environment variables

All plugins receive these environment variables during execution:

| Variable               | Description                                  |
|------------------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `SEMREL_VERSION`       | semrel CLI version                           |
| `SEMREL_TAG_NAME`      | Full tag name (e.g. `v1.3.0`)                |
| `SEMREL_CURRENT_VERSION` | Current project version                    |
| `SEMREL_NEXT_VERSION`  | Next version determined by the analyzer      |
| `SEMREL_BUMP`          | Bump level: `major`, `minor`, or `patch`     |
| `SEMREL_BRANCH`        | Current git branch                           |
| `SEMREL_TAG_PREFIX`    | Configured tag prefix                        |
| `SEMREL_CHANGELOG`     | Generated changelog content                  |
| `SEMREL_DRY_RUN`       | `true` if running in dry-run mode            |
| `SEMREL_PLUGIN_<KEY>`  | Plugin-specific args from `args:` block      |

---

## Plugin categories

| Category  | Purpose                                                                 |
|-----------|-------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| Provider  | Forge integration: create tag, publish release, upload assets           |
| Condition | Guard: allow or block release based on CI environment                   |
| Analyzer  | Commit analysis: determine SemVer bump level                            |
| Generator | Produce changelog, release notes                                        |
| Updater   | Update version files before tagging                                     |
| Hook      | Post-release notifications and automation                               |

---

## Official plugins

### Providers
- **provider-github** — GitHub Releases via the GitHub API
- **provider-gitlab** — GitLab Releases via the GitLab API
- **provider-gitea** — Gitea Releases via the Gitea API
- **provider-bitbucket** — Bitbucket Cloud (tags + pipeline integration)
- **provider-git** — Plain git: tag only, no hosted release API

### Conditions
- **condition-github-actions** — Allow release only on GitHub Actions (main/master)
- **condition-gitea-actions** — Gitea Actions equivalent
- **condition-gitlab-ci** — GitLab CI/CD pipeline equivalent
- **condition-generic** — Configurable condition via environment variable matching

### Analyzers
- **analyzer-conventional** — Full Conventional Commits spec, supports scopes and footers
- **analyzer-default** — Simplified prefix-based analysis (`feat:`, `fix:`, `break:`)

### Generators
- **generator-changelog-md** — Markdown CHANGELOG.md, grouped by type
- **generator-changelog-html** — HTML changelog for GitHub Releases body
- **generator-release-notes** — Standalone release notes document

### Updaters
- **updater-go** — Updates `go.mod` module version
- **updater-npm** — Updates `package.json` version
- **updater-cargo** — Updates `Cargo.toml` version
- **updater-docker** — Updates Dockerfile label / ARG VERSION
- **updater-helm** — Updates `Chart.yaml` appVersion
- **updater-maven** — Updates `pom.xml` version
- **updater-gradle** — Updates `build.gradle` / `gradle.properties` version
- **updater-python** — Updates `pyproject.toml` / `setup.py` version
- **updater-nuget** — Updates `.csproj` version
- **updater-terraform** — Updates `version.tf` / `main.tf` module version
- **updater-homebrew** — Updates Homebrew formula version and SHA256

### Hooks
- **hook-slack** — Slack incoming webhook notification
- **hook-teams** — Microsoft Teams incoming webhook
- **hook-email** — SMTP email notification
- **hook-jira** — Jira issue transition / comment
- **hook-matrix** — Matrix chat room message
- **hook-gitplugin** — Git-based post-release automation

---

## Installing semrel

### Go install
```bash
go install github.com/SemRels/semrel@latest
```

### Homebrew (macOS / Linux)
```bash
brew install semrels/tap/semrel
```

### Docker
```bash
docker run --rm -v "$PWD":/workspace ghcr.io/semrels/semrel:latest release
```

### Binary download
Download from https://github.com/SemRels/semrel/releases — available for linux/amd64,
linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64, windows/amd64.

---

## Installing plugins

```bash
semrel plugin install github          # installs provider-github
semrel plugin install @semrel/slack   # installs hook-slack from the registry
semrel plugin list                    # shows installed plugins
semrel plugin restore                 # restores from .semrel.lock
```

Plugins are downloaded to `.semrel/plugins/` and pinned in `.semrel.lock`.

---

## Monorepo usage

Create a `.semrel.yaml` in each module directory:

```
my-repo/
  services/
    api/
      .semrel.yaml   # tag prefix: services/api/v
    worker/
      .semrel.yaml   # tag prefix: services/worker/v
```

Run from each module directory or use:
```bash
semrel release --config services/api/.semrel.yaml
```

---

## Plugin Registry

The semrel Plugin Registry at https://registry.semrel.io is a hosted index of official and
community plugins. It exposes a JSON REST API:

- `GET /api/v1/plugins` — list all active plugins (paginated, filterable by category/search)
- `GET /api/v1/plugins/:id` — single plugin metadata
- `GET /api/v1/plugins/:id/versions` — plugin version history
- `GET /api/v1/plugins/@namespace/name` — namespaced lookup

---

## Frequently Asked Questions

**Q: Is semrel production-ready?**
A: Yes. It is used in production across multiple organizations. Official plugins are versioned,
signed, and have documented SBOM provenance.

**Q: Does semrel require Node.js?**
A: No. semrel is a single static Go binary with zero Node.js dependency. Plugins are also
standalone binaries.

**Q: Can I write a plugin in Python?**
A: Yes. Any executable that reads environment variables and returns the correct exit code is
a valid semrel plugin.

**Q: How does semrel differ from semantic-release?**
A: semantic-release is Node.js-based and uses a JavaScript plugin ecosystem. semrel is a
Go binary, uses subprocess-based plugins in any language, and has stronger supply-chain
security defaults. semrel is designed for Go projects but supports all ecosystems.

**Q: Does semrel support private repositories?**
A: Yes. All provider plugins accept tokens via environment variables and work with private
repositories on GitHub, GitLab, Gitea, and Bitbucket.

**Q: What is the license?**
A: Apache 2.0. See https://github.com/SemRels/semrel/blob/main/LICENSE.
